text: Broker Amy Adams sends 84.3 percent of her referrals to Carlson Medical Centre, but supplies only 8.4 percent of that large clinic's claims, and transfers exceed expected commission by 6.5 percent on 278,376 dollars of billing. One-way dependence — a small broker leaning on a big accredited hospital — is the classic honest asymmetry, which is why this stays low. There is no stake and no address sharing. The modest excess margin is worth a routine reconciliation, nothing more. Next step: batch the commission-schedule check with the other low kickback alerts.
